headline: Daily research brief — Monday, October 12

items.detail: TSLA reports Q3 2026 Wed Oct 21 after close (webcast 5:30 PM ET). The Oct-23 ATM straddle mid of 15.00 on a 378.03 underlying implies ±3.97% (Yahoo chain, crumb-authenticated, 1:00 PM ET), versus ±5.95% average-absolute over the last four earnings sessions — including a −14.5% drop in July. Signed average −4.81%. The print has not driven the move this year (July's drop followed a record delivery quarter); the desk's Oct 21 work starts at auto gross margin, GAAP vs adjusted, OCF vs net income, and Q4 guidance. Premium into this event = avoid.
items.title: TSLA Oct 21 is the only in-window binary — options price it below its recent base rate

items.detail: IRGC Navy reports three tankers struck naval mines Oct 10–12 near Hormuz (one-sided claims — no independent vessel identification as of deadline, UNVERIFIED); Houthis claimed airport strikes in Riyadh/Dammam (aviation, not energy infrastructure). Dec Brent settled $106.65 (+1.8%), Nov WTI $93.74 (+2.1%); the Brent-WTI spread widened to $12.86, concentrating the premium in seaborne barrels. VLCC Persian Gulf→East Asia rates are at a record ~$1.4M/day. The curve's long end ($50s–$60s) prices a contained disruption, not a structural re-rating — any credible de-escalation headline is the asymmetric move lower. Goldman raised its Dec Brent forecast to $90 (from $85), estimating >$20/bbl geopolitical risk premium.
items.title: Weekend escalation is the live oil catalyst — Brent $106.65 in steep backwardation

items.detail: Corn yield 181.2 bpa vs ~177.6 expected (the trade positioned for a cut), production 16,034M bu (second-largest on record), ending stocks 1,849 mb (+282 mb m/m), farm price cut to $4.70 — Dec corn briefly hit limit-down Friday. Soybeans were near-neutral, saved by Chinese buying (+4.5¢ to $12.94). Wheat ending stocks rose to 740 mb despite the smallest U.S. crop since 1970; exports cut on 32% y/y lower commitments. Next reads: EIA Wed Oct 14 (10:30 ET; Reuters consensus poll not yet published — UNVERIFIED) and Nov WASDE Nov 10.
items.title: October WASDE was a bearish corn event — USDA raised yield when the trade expected a cut

items.detail: FRED through Oct 8 (live, no data blackout): EFFR 3.88%, 2Y 4.75%, 10Y 5.22%, 2s-10s +47bp — both ends sold off ~60bp in parallel since mid-August, a bear shift, not a slope change. 2Y/10Y peaked Oct 5 (4.84/5.31) and eased into Oct 8 — a modest tailwind into earnings season; a re-test of 5.30%+ flips back to headwind. SOFR minus EFFR −1bp: secured and unsecured funding rates essentially identical, no disorderly-liquidity signal. Elevated long rates keep the margin-of-safety bar high for growth names (QQQ, NVDA, TSLA most exposed).
items.title: Rates steady in higher-for-longer territory — 10Y 5.22%, no funding stress
